title: Anxiety: A Heart Issue
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Thesis of the Series
subpoints: Anxiety is a heart issue, not primarily a medical one
The solution lies in focusing on God's attributes
Shifting from a clinical victimhood view to a Godward view

outline.title: Reasons for Studying Anxiety
subpoints: Anxiety is prevalent across all demographics
Culture often misplaces anxiety in the realm of disease
The Bible provides extensive teaching on this topic
Correct categorization leads to true hope and solution

outline.title: Locating the Origin of Anxiety
subpoints: Popular wisdom views anxiety as a brain-body disease
The biblical model views it as a heart/inner self issue
The individual is an active responder, not a helpless victim
Anxiety is a response of the heart to circumstances or thoughts

outline.title: The Inner and Outer Man
subpoints: The outer man is the physical body, subject to decay
The inner man is the spiritual self, renewed by the Word
Physical decline does not necessitate spiritual decline
Bodies cannot force the soul to sin or be anxious

summary:
In this introductory session of a nine-part series on anxiety, Pastor Tito Lyro establishes the central thesis that anxiety is fundamentally a heart issue rather than a purely medical disorder. He argues that contrary to popular clinical views which categorize anxiety as a brain-body disease requiring medication, the biblical perspective identifies it as a matter of the inner man. This shift in perspective moves the individual from the status of a helpless victim to that of an active responder who can address the root cause through spiritual means.

The pastor outlines four primary reasons for addressing this topic: the widespread prevalence of anxiety among all demographics, the cultural tendency to misplace anxiety in the realm of pathology, the extensive biblical teaching on the subject, and the availability of true hope when the problem is correctly categorized. By locating anxiety in the heart, the solution becomes one of repentance, faith, and a godward focus rather than solely medical intervention.

Drawing on 2 Corinthians 4:16, the sermon distinguishes between the outer man (the physical body) and the inner man (the spiritual self). While the outer man is subject to decay and physical limitations, the inner man is renewed day by day through the Word of God. This distinction is crucial for understanding that physical circumstances or bodily states do not necessitate spiritual failure or anxiety; rather, anxiety is a response of the heart to life's situations, which can be addressed by meditating on the attributes of God.
